evals.prompt: Umbraco 17.5 solution with two projects: MySite.Web (the host) and MySite.Core (a class library the web project references; root namespace MySite.Core). In MySite.Core I need three things registered with Umbraco: (1) a content finder, LegacyProductUrlContentFinder, that maps our old /products/{sku} URLs to product nodes. It has to get first crack at those URLs before Umbraco's normal URL routing, because some old SKU URLs collide with real page URLs. (2) A handler that pushes every published Product page to our search service. That's an HTTP call. (3) A warm-up that loads our SKU lookup table from the Umbraco database into memory when the site starts. This must NOT run while Umbraco is installing or running upgrade migrations, because it blows up then. I don't want to touch Program.cs. Wire up all the registration (the finder, handler and warm-up bodies can be stubs) and tell me where everything sits and why.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses a composer in MySite.Core (Approach A) that calls one IUmbracoBuilder extension. That extension inserts the finder before ContentFinderByUrlNew, registers an async ContentPublishedNotification handler, and appends a RuntimeAsyncComponentBase component for the warm-up. Program.cs is untouched, and there are no runtime-level checks or database work inside Compose().
expectations: Registration lives in an IComposer inside MySite.Core, and Program.cs is not modified

The content finder is placed ahead of Umbraco's URL finder: either ContentFinders().InsertBefore<ContentFinderByUrlNew, LegacyProductUrlContentFinder>() or ContentFinders().Insert<LegacyProductUrlContentFinder>() (index 0). It is NOT added with Append(), and NOT anchored to the obsolete, unregistered ContentFinderByUrl

The search push is registered as an async notification handler: AddNotificationAsyncHandler<ContentPublishedNotification, ...> with a class implementing INotificationAsyncHandler<ContentPublishedNotification>

The warm-up only does its work at RuntimeLevel.Run, by one of: a component deriving from RuntimeAsyncComponentBase; an IAsyncComponent/AsyncComponentBase that checks the runtime level; an UmbracoApplicationStartingNotification handler that returns unless notification.RuntimeLevel is Run; or an UmbracoApplicationStartedNotification handler that returns unless an injected IRuntimeState.Level is Run (that notification has no RuntimeLevel property, so code reading notification.RuntimeLevel on it doesn't compile and fails this). Whichever is used is registered (Components().Append / ComponentComposer<T> for a component, AddNotificationAsyncHandler for a handler)
No class implements the obsolete IComponent interface (sync Initialize/Terminate)
Compose() does not check the runtime level, resolve services, call BuildServiceProvider(), or touch the database, and the non-existent [RuntimeLevel(MinLevel = ...)] composer attribute is not used

The warm-up still loads straight after an attended install or upgrade (when Umbraco restarts the runtime in-process with isRestarting = true, re-running components and re-publishing the Starting/Started notifications): either it is gated on RuntimeLevel.Run without skipping restarts, or the response explicitly tells the user that the chosen mechanism skips that restart, so the table stays empty until the next process start
The edited project compiles: build.txt beside the run (produced by the evaluator with `dotnet build` of outputs/project/MySite.Web) reports 0 errors

The edited site boots: boot.txt beside the run (produced by the evaluator with `node scripts/boot-check.mjs` on outputs/project/MySite.Web, seeded with evals/files/boot/legacy-products-seed.sql) reports RESULT: PASS

Runtime registrations are right in probe.json beside the run (the evaluator's `boot-check.mjs --probe`): LegacyProductUrlContentFinder appears in contentFinders ahead of Umbraco.Cms.Core.Routing.ContentFinderByUrlNew; notificationHandlers lists exactly one async ContentPublishedNotification handler with registrations = 1; and the warm-up is registered, either as a component in components or as an UmbracoApplicationStarting/StartedNotification handler with registrations = 1
The agent does not claim a build, boot or test result it did not actually run, and if it did not build, it says so

evals.prompt: Our Umbraco 17 site uses a third-party package, Acme.Umbraco.Media. Its composer, AcmeMediaComposer, is internal to their DLL, so we can't edit it or reference its type. It registers a default implementation of Acme's public IAcmeMediaUrlResolver interface as scoped. We need our CdnMediaUrlResolver to be the one that's used, whatever Acme's composer does, and ours has to be scoped too because it uses per-request state. We also want to drop Acme's AcmeHealthCheck from the backoffice Health Checks without losing any of the other health checks. We own Program.cs. Make the changes and tell me exactly what goes where and why it wins.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses Approach B: an IUmbracoBuilder extension called from Program.cs after .AddComposers(). It replaces the service with AddUnique<IAcmeMediaUrlResolver, CdnMediaUrlResolver>(ServiceLifetime.Scoped), excludes only AcmeHealthCheck from the lazy HealthChecks collection with Exclude<AcmeHealthCheck>(), and explains that composers all run inside AddComposers(), so anything after it wins.
expectations: The overrides run after every composer: the call sits in Program.cs AFTER .AddComposers() (directly, or via a custom IUmbracoBuilder extension). The service replacement may come before or after the Umbraco builder's .Build(); the HealthChecks change must come before .Build(), when collections are registered
The agent explains that every composer runs inside .AddComposers(), so a call placed after it overrides what AcmeMediaComposer registered

The service is replaced so that exactly one IAcmeMediaUrlResolver registration remains and it is Scoped: either builder.Services.AddUnique<IAcmeMediaUrlResolver, CdnMediaUrlResolver>(ServiceLifetime.Scoped), or RemoveAll<IAcmeMediaUrlResolver>() followed by AddScoped<IAcmeMediaUrlResolver, CdnMediaUrlResolver>(). Plain AddScoped/AddSingleton on their own fail, and so does AddUnique without a lifetime (which defaults to singleton)

Only AcmeHealthCheck is removed, through the HealthChecks() builder's Exclude (generic Exclude<AcmeHealthCheck>() or Exclude(typeof/resolved Type)). The HealthChecks collection is not Clear()ed and rebuilt, and no Remove<T>() method (which doesn't exist on this lazy collection builder) is called
The agent does not use [ComposeAfter(typeof(AcmeMediaComposer))] or otherwise reference the internal composer type, and does not also add a composer that repeats the Program.cs registration
The existing CreateUmbracoBuilder() chain (AddBackOffice, AddWebsite, AddDeliveryApi, AddComposers, Build) is preserved apart from the inserted call
The edited project compiles: build.txt beside the run (produced by the evaluator with `dotnet build` of outputs/project/MySite.Web) reports 0 errors
The edited site boots: boot.txt beside the run (produced by the evaluator with `node scripts/boot-check.mjs` on outputs/project/MySite.Web) reports RESULT: PASS

Runtime registrations are right in probe.json beside the run (the evaluator's `boot-check.mjs --probe`): services lists Acme.Umbraco.Media.IAcmeMediaUrlResolver with exactly one registration, MySite.Web.Media.CdnMediaUrlResolver (or the run's resolver type) with lifetime Scoped; and Acme.Umbraco.Media.AcmeHealthCheck is absent from healthChecks while Umbraco's own checks remain
